key_insight: Hyperlyve combines learning with formal verification to certify that nonlinear systems, including those controlled by neural networks, converge toward an equilibrium. Its central innovation is parallel enumeration of the regions induced by ReLU activation boundaries.
problem_solved: A neural controller can perform well in tests without guaranteeing stability. Hyperlyve addresses the challenge of constructing and formally certifying neural Lyapunov functions rather than relying only on sampled behavior.
method: Learn continuous piecewise-affine neural Lyapunov functions as candidates for proving asymptotic stability.
Use a parallel algorithm to enumerate the hyperplane-partitioned regions associated with ReLU activations.
Refine candidates through a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis loop, alternating learning and formal certification.
impact: Hyperlyve provides a route toward rigorous stability guarantees for neural-network-controlled systems. Parallel enumeration targets a computational bottleneck in analyzing piecewise-affine neural functions.

paper_title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
paper_authors: Brian Yarbrough, Jesse Wayment, Jingbo Wang, Philip E. Paré, Shreyas Sundaram
